sanskrit: atha jitvā maruttaṃ sa prayayau rākṣasādhipaḥ nagarāṇi narendrāṇāṃ yuddhakāṅkṣī daśānanaḥ
english: Having vanquished Marutta, the lord of rākṣasas, the ten-faced Daśānana, ever eager for battle, then marched against the cities of other kings.

sanskrit: sa samāsādya rājendrān mahendravaruṇopamān abravīd rākṣasendras tu yuddhaṃ me dīyatām iti
english: Approaching those royal lords, who were comparable to Mahendra and Varuṇa, the king of rākṣasas declared: "Give me battle."

sanskrit: nirjitāḥ smeti vā brūta eṣo hi mama niścayaḥ anyathā kurvatām evaṃ mokṣo vo nopapadyate
english: "Or else say, 'We are conquered' — that is my firm resolve. For those who do otherwise, there shall be no escape."

sanskrit: tatas tu bahavaḥ prājñāḥ pārthivā dharmaṇiścayāḥ nirjitāḥ smety abhāṣanta jñātvā varabalaṃ ripoḥ
english: Thereupon many wise kings, firm in righteousness, declared "We are conquered," recognizing the superior power of their foe.

sanskrit: duṣyantaḥ suratho gādhir gayo rājā purūravāḥ ete sarve 'bruvaṃs tāta nirjitāḥ smeti pārthivāḥ
english: Duṣyanta, Suratha, Gādhi, King Gaya, and Purūravas — all these kings declared, O friend, "We are conquered."

sanskrit: athāyodhyāṃ samāsādya rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ suguptām anaraṇyena śakreṇevāmarāvatīm
english: Then Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, approached Ayodhyā, well-guarded by Anaraṇya as Amarāvatī is guarded by Śakra.

sanskrit: prāha rājānam āsādya yuddhaṃ me saṃpradīyatām nirjito 'smīti vā brūhi mamaitad iha śāsanam
english: He addressed the king: "Give me battle, or else say 'I am conquered' — such is my command here."

sanskrit: anaraṇyaḥ susaṃkruddho rākṣasendram athābravīt dīyate dvandvayuddhaṃ te rākṣasādhipate mayā
english: Then Anaraṇya, greatly enraged, replied to the lord of rākṣasas: "I grant you single combat, O lord of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: atha pūrvaṃ śrutārthena sajjitaṃ sumahad dhi yat niṣkrāmat tan narendrasya balaṃ rakṣovadhodyatam
english: Then that great army of the king, which had been assembled in advance upon hearing the purpose and was prepared, sallied forth intent on slaying the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: nāgānāṃ bahusāhasraṃ vājinām ayutaṃ tathā mahīṃ saṃchādya niṣkrāntaṃ sapadātirathaṃ kṣaṇāt
english: Many thousands of elephants and ten thousand horses, together with infantry and chariots, poured forth instantly, covering the earth.

sanskrit: tad rāvaṇabalaṃ prāpya balaṃ tasya mahīpateḥ prāṇaśyata tadā rājan havyaṃ hutam ivānale
english: Upon meeting Rāvaṇa's force, the army of that lord of the earth was annihilated, O king, like an oblation cast into fire.

sanskrit: so 'paśyata narendras tu naśyamānaṃ mahad balam mahārṇavaṃ samāsādya yathā pañcāpagā jalam
english: The king watched his great army being destroyed, as five rivers are swallowed up when they reach the great ocean.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakradhanuḥprakhyaṃ dhanur visphārayan svayam āsadāda narendrās taṃ rāvaṇaṃ krodhamūrchitaḥ
english: Then that king, overwhelmed with rage, himself drawing his bow — brilliant as the bow of Indra — advanced against Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tato bāṇaśatāny aṣṭau pātayām āsa mūrdhani tasya rākṣasarājasya ikṣvākukulanandanaḥ
english: The joy of the Ikṣvāku line let fly eight hundred arrows at the head of that king of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tasya bāṇāḥ patantas te cakrire na kṣataṃ kva cit vāridhārā ivābhrebhyaḥ patantyo nagamūrdhani
english: But those arrows, as they fell, made no wound anywhere upon him — like streams of water falling from clouds upon the summit of a mountain.

sanskrit: tato rākṣasarājena kruddhena nṛpatis tadā talena bhihato mūrdhni sa rathān nipapāta ha
english: Then the enraged king of rākṣasas struck the king with his palm upon the head, and the king fell from his chariot.

sanskrit: sa rājā patito bhūmau vihvalāṅgaḥ pravepitaḥ vajradagdha ivāraṇye sālo nipatito mahān
english: That king fell to the ground, his limbs convulsed and trembling, like a great sāla tree felled in the forest by a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: taṃ prahasyābravīd rakṣa ikṣvākuṃ pṛthivīpatim kim idānīṃ tvayā prāptaṃ phalaṃ māṃ prati yudhyatā
english: Laughing, the rākṣasa addressed that Ikṣvāku lord of the earth: "What fruit have you now obtained by fighting against me?"

sanskrit: trailokye nāsti yo dvandvaṃ mama dadyān narādhipa śaṅke pramatto bhogeṣu na śṛṇoṣi balaṃ mama
english: "There is none in the three worlds who could give me single combat, O king. I think that, heedless in your pleasures, you have not heard of my might."

sanskrit: tasyaivaṃ bruvato rājā mandāsur vākyam abravīt kiṃ śakyam iha kartuṃ vai yat kālo duratikramaḥ
english: As he spoke thus, the king, his breath fading, replied: "What can be done here, when time is insurmountable?"

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ nirjito rakṣas tvayā cātmapraśaṃsinā kāleneha vipanno 'haṃ hetubhūtas tu me bhavān
english: "I have not been conquered by you, O rākṣasa, self-lauding one — I have been undone by time. You are merely the instrument of my fall."

sanskrit: kiṃ tv idānīṃ mayā śakyaṃ kartuṃ prāṇaparikṣaye ikṣvākuparibhāvitvād vaco vakṣyāmi rākṣasa
english: "Yet what can I now do when my life is ebbing away? Because of the dishonor done to the Ikṣvākus, I shall speak these words, O rākṣasa:"

sanskrit: yadi dattaṃ yadi hutaṃ yadi me sukṛtaṃ tapaḥ yadi guptāḥ prajāḥ samyak tathā satyaṃ vaco 'stu me
english: "If I have given gifts, if I have made oblations, if I have performed austerities rightly, if I have protected my subjects well — then let my words be true:"

sanskrit: utpatsyate kule hy asminn ikṣvākūṇāṃ mahātmanām rājā paramatejasvī yas te prāṇān hariṣyati
english: "In this very line of the great-souled Ikṣvākus shall be born a king of supreme splendor who will take your life."

sanskrit: tato jaladharodagras tāḍito devadundubhiḥ tasminn udāhṛte śāpe puṣpavṛṣṭiś ca khāc cyutā
english: Then, when that curse had been uttered, the divine kettledrums resounded like towering rain-clouds being struck, and a rain of flowers fell from the sky.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā rājendra gataḥ sthānaṃ triviṣṭapam svargate ca nṛpe rāma rākṣasaḥ sa nyavartata
english: Then that king, O king of kings, went to his place in the heavenly realm; and when the king had gone to heaven, O Rāma, the rākṣasa turned away.

sanskrit: tato vitrāsayan martyān pṛthivyāṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ āsasāda ghane tasmin nāradaṃ munisattamam
english: Then, as he terrorized mortals upon the earth, the lord of rākṣasas encountered in that thick region the foremost of sages, Nārada.

sanskrit: nāradas tu mahātejā devarṣir amitaprabhaḥ abravīn meghapṛṣṭhastho rāvaṇaṃ puṣpake sthitam
english: Nārada, the divine sage of great splendor and boundless radiance, standing upon a cloud, addressed Rāvaṇa, who was seated in the Puṣpaka.

sanskrit: rākṣasādhipate saumya tiṣṭha viśravasaḥ suta prīto 'smy abhijanopeta vikramair ūrjitais tava
english: "O lord of rākṣasas, gentle one, halt, O son of Viśravas. I am pleased with your mighty exploits and your noble lineage."

sanskrit: viṣṇunā daityaghātaiś ca tārkṣyasyoragadharṣaṇaiḥ tvayā samaramardaiś ca bhṛśaṃ hi paritoṣitaḥ
english: "By Viṣṇu with his slaughter of daityas, by Tārkṣya with his routing of serpents, and by you with your crushing of foes in battle — I am greatly gratified."

sanskrit: kiṃ cid vakṣyāmi tāvat te śrotavyaṃ śroṣyase yadi śrutvā cānantaraṃ kāryaṃ tvayā rākṣasapuṃgava
english: "I shall say something that deserves to be heard — will you hear it? And having heard it, you should act accordingly, O bull among rākṣasas."

sanskrit: kim ayaṃ vadhyate lokas tvayāvadhyena daivataiḥ hata eva hy ayaṃ loko yadā mṛtyuvaśaṃ gataḥ
english: "Why do you slay this world, you who cannot be slain by the gods? This world is already slain when it has fallen under the power of death."

sanskrit: paśya tāvan mahābāho rākṣaseśvaramānuṣam lokam enaṃ vicitrārthaṃ yasya na jñāyate gatiḥ
english: "Behold first, O mighty-armed lord of rākṣasas, this human world, wondrous in its purposes, whose course cannot be known."

sanskrit: kva cid vāditranṛttāni sevyante muditair janaiḥ rudyate cāparair ārtair dhārāśrunayanānanaiḥ
english: "In one place, music and dancing are enjoyed by people full of joy; elsewhere others weep in grief, their faces streaming with tears."

sanskrit: mātā pitṛsutasnehair bhāryā bandhumanoramaiḥ mohenāyaṃ jano dhvastaḥ kleśaṃ svaṃ nāvabudhyate
english: "Bound by the affections of mother, father, son, wife, and cherished kinsmen, this people is ruined by delusion and does not perceive its own suffering."

sanskrit: tat kim evaṃ parikliśya lokaṃ mohanirākṛtam jita eva tvayā saumya martyaloko na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Why then afflict this world already undone by delusion? The mortal world is conquered by you already, O gentle one — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu laṅkeśo dīpyamāna ivaujasā abravīn nāradaṃ tatra saṃprahasyābhivādya ca
english: Thus addressed, the lord of Laṅkā, blazing as it were with energy, laughed aloud and, saluting Nārada, spoke to him there.

sanskrit: maharṣe devagandharvavihāra samarapriya ahaṃ khalūdyato gantuṃ vijayārthī rasātalam
english: "O great sage, you who roam among gods and gandharvas, you who love battle — I am indeed setting out to descend to the netherworld in quest of victory."

sanskrit: tato lokatrayaṃ jitvā sthāpya nāgān surān vaśe samudram amṛtārthaṃ vai mathiṣyāmi rasālayam
english: "Having conquered the three worlds and brought nāgas and gods under my sway, I shall then churn the ocean, that abode of nectar, for the sake of amṛta."

sanskrit: athābravīd daśagrīvaṃ nārado bhagavān ṛṣiḥ kva khalv idānīṃ mārgeṇa tvayānena gamiṣyate
english: Then the blessed sage Nārada addressed the ten-necked one: "By which route now are you going?"

sanskrit: ayaṃ khalu sudurgamyaḥ pitṛrājñaḥ puraṃ prati mārgo gacchati durdharṣo yamasyāmitrakarśana
english: "This route to the city of the king of the dead is exceedingly hard to traverse, O crusher of foes — it leads to Yama's domain and is most formidable."

sanskrit: sa tu śāradameghābhaṃ muktvā hāsaṃ daśānanaḥ uvāca kṛtam ity eva vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: But Daśānana released a laugh like an autumnal cloud and, saying "Very well," spoke these words.

sanskrit: tasmād eṣa mahābrahman vaivasvatavadhodyataḥ gacchāmi dakṣiṇām āśāṃ yatra sūryātmajo nṛpaḥ
english: "Therefore, O great brahmin, I am proceeding in the southern direction, intent on slaying Vaivasvata, where the son of the Sun holds sway as king."

sanskrit: mayā hi bhagavan krodhāt pratijñātaṃ raṇārthinā avajeṣyāmi caturo lokapālān iti prabho
english: "For I have vowed in anger, O blessed one, seeking battle, that I will vanquish the four guardians of the worlds, O lord."

sanskrit: tenaiṣa prasthito 'haṃ vai pitṛrājapuraṃ prati prāṇisaṃkleśakartāraṃ yojayiṣyāmi mṛtyunā
english: "For that reason I am now proceeding to the city of the king of the ancestors — I shall join with death that one who brings affliction to all living beings."

sanskrit: evam uktvā daśagrīvo muniṃ tam abhivādya ca prayayau dakṣiṇām āśāṃ prahṛṣṭaiḥ saha mantribhiḥ
english: Having spoken thus and saluting the sage, Daśagrīva departed toward the southern quarter together with his exultant ministers.

sanskrit: nāradas tu mahātejā muhūrtaṃ dhyānam āsthitaḥ cintayām āsa viprendro vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ
english: Then Nārada, the foremost of seers, of great splendor, entered into meditation for a moment and reflected, like fire without smoke.

sanskrit: yena lokās trayaḥ sendrāḥ kliśyante sacarācarāḥ kṣīṇe cāyuṣi dharme ca sa kālo hiṃsyate katham
english: "He by whom the three worlds, with Indra, with all moving and unmoving beings, are afflicted — and when life-span and dharma are diminished — how is that time-force itself to be destroyed?"

sanskrit: yasya nityaṃ trayo lokā vidravanti bhayārditāḥ taṃ kathaṃ rākṣasendro 'sau svayam evābhigacchati
english: "He from whom the three worlds always flee in terror — how is it that this lord of rākṣasas goes of his own accord toward him?"

sanskrit: yo vidhātā ca dhātā ca sukṛte duṣkṛte yathā trailokyaṃ vijitaṃ yena taṃ kathaṃ nu vijeṣyati
english: "He who is both ordainer and arranger for merit and demerit alike, by whom the three worlds are already conquered — how indeed shall he conquer him?"

sanskrit: aparaṃ kiṃ nu kṛtvaivaṃ vidhānaṃ saṃvidhāsyati kautūhalasamutpanno yāsyāmi yamasādanam
english: "What arrangement will be made differently from this? Stirred by curiosity, I shall go to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃcintya viprendro jagāma laghuvikramaḥ ākhyātuṃ tad yathāvṛttaṃ yamasya sadanaṃ prati
english: Having thus reflected, the foremost of seers, swift in valor, went toward the abode of Yama to report what had transpired.

sanskrit: apaśyat sa yamaṃ tatra devam agnipuraskṛtam vidhānam upatiṣṭhantaṃ prāṇino yasya yādṛśam
english: There he saw the god Yama, attended by fire, presiding over the ordained fate of each living being according to its kind.

sanskrit: sa tu dṛṣṭvā yamaḥ prāptaṃ maharṣiṃ tatra nāradam abravīt sukham āsīnam arghyam āvedya dharmataḥ
english: Seeing the great sage Nārada arrived there, Yama offered him arghya according to the rites and, when the sage was comfortably seated, addressed him.

sanskrit: kaccit kṣemaṃ nu devarṣe kaccid dharmo na naśyati kim āgamanakṛtyaṃ te devagandharvasevita
english: "Is all well, O divine sage? Is dharma not perishing? What is the purpose of your coming, O one honored by gods and gandharvas?"

sanskrit: abravīt tu tadā vākyaṃ nārado bhagavān ṛṣiḥ śrūyatām abhidhāsyāmi vidhānaṃ ca vidhīyatām
english: Then the blessed sage Nārada spoke: "Hear what I shall say, and let the proper arrangement be made."

sanskrit: eṣa nāmnā daśagrīvaḥ pitṛrāja niśācaraḥ upayāti vaśaṃ netuṃ vikramais tvāṃ sudurjayam
english: "This night-wanderer, named Daśagrīva, O king of the ancestors, is coming by force to bring you, most difficult to conquer, under his sway."

sanskrit: etena kāraṇenāhaṃ tvarito 'smy āgataḥ prabho daṇḍapraharaṇasyādya tava kiṃ nu kariṣyati
english: "For this reason I have come hastily, O lord. What will he now do against your rod of punishment?"

sanskrit: etasminn antare dūrād aṃśumantam ivoditam dadṛśe divyam āyāntaṃ vimānaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: In that very interval, from afar the divine aerial vehicle of that rākṣasa was seen approaching — blazing like the risen sun.

sanskrit: taṃ deśaṃ prabhayā tasya puṣpakasya mahābalaḥ kṛtvā vitimiraṃ sarvaṃ samīpaṃ samavartata
english: That mighty one, with the radiance of the Puṣpaka, having dispelled all darkness from that region, drew near.

sanskrit: sa tv apaśyan mahābāhur daśagrīvas tatas tataḥ prāṇinaḥ sukṛtaṃ karma bhuñjānāṃś caiva duṣkṛtam
english: The mighty-armed Daśagrīva looked about here and there and saw living beings reaping the fruits of their good deeds and of their evil deeds.

sanskrit: tatas tān vadhyamānāṃs tu karmabhir duṣkṛtaiḥ svakaiḥ rāvaṇo mocayām āsa vikrameṇa balād balī
english: Then Rāvaṇa, the powerful one, by his own valor forcibly released those who were being tormented by their own evil deeds.

sanskrit: preteṣu mucyamāneṣu rākṣasena balīyasā pretagopāḥ susaṃrabdhā rākṣasendram abhidravan
english: As the dead were being freed by that most powerful rākṣasa, the guardians of the dead, greatly enraged, rushed toward the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: te prāsaiḥ parighaiḥ śūlair mudgaraiḥ śaktitomaraiḥ puṣpakaṃ samavarṣanta śūrāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: Those warriors, hundreds of thousands in number, showered the Puṣpaka with javelins, iron clubs, spears, mallets, śaktis, and tomaras.

sanskrit: tasyāsanāni prāsādān vedikāstaraṇāni ca puṣpakasya babhañjus te śīghraṃ madhukarā iva
english: They swiftly shattered the seats, pavilions, balustrades, and coverings of the Puṣpaka, like bees swarming upon it.

sanskrit: devaniṣṭhānabhūtaṃ tad vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ mṛdhe bhajyamānaṃ tathaivāsīd akṣayaṃ brahmatejasā
english: Yet that celestial craft, the Puṣpaka — though shattered in battle — remained indestructible nonetheless, by virtue of Brahmā's divine power.

sanskrit: tatas te rāvaṇāmātyā yathākāmaṃ yathābalam ayudhyanta mahāvīryāḥ sa ca rājā daśānanaḥ
english: Then Rāvaṇa's ministers, those of great valor, fought with all their will and all their strength, and so too did the king Daśānana himself.

sanskrit: te tu śoṇitadigdhāṅgāḥ sarvaśastrasamāhatāḥ amātyā rākṣasendrasya cakrur āyodhanaṃ mahat
english: Those ministers of the lord of rākṣasas, their limbs smeared with blood and battered by every weapon, waged a mighty battle.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ ca mahābhāgā jaghnuḥ praharaṇair yudhi yamasya ca mahat sainyaṃ rākṣasasya ca mantriṇaḥ
english: The great ones struck one another in battle with their weapons; the great army of Yama and the ministers of the rākṣasa lord smote each other.

sanskrit: amātyāṃs tāṃs tu saṃtyajya rākṣasasya mahaujasaḥ tam eva samadhāvanta śūlavarṣair daśānanam
english: Leaving aside those ministers of the mighty rākṣasa, they charged toward Daśānana himself, raining spears upon him.

sanskrit: tataḥ śoṇitadigdhāṅgaḥ prahārair jarjarīkṛtaḥ vimāne rākṣasaśreṣṭhaḥ phullāśoka ivābabhau
english: Then the foremost of rākṣasas, his limbs smeared with blood and riddled with blows, shone upon his aerial vehicle like a blossoming aśoka tree.

sanskrit: sa śūlāni gadāḥ prāsāñ śaktitomarasāyakān musalāni śilāvṛkṣān mumocāstrabalād balī
english: That powerful one released by force of arms spears, maces, javelins, śaktis, tomaras, arrows, pestles, rocks, and trees.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu sarvān samākṣipya tad astram apahatya ca jaghnus te rākṣasaṃ ghoram ekaṃ śatasahasrakaḥ
english: But gathering up all those missiles and neutralizing those weapons, they — a hundred thousand against one — struck that terrible rākṣasa.

sanskrit: parivārya ca taṃ sarve śailaṃ meghotkarā iva bhindipālaiś ca śūlaiś ca nirucchvāsam akārayan
english: Surrounding him on all sides like massed clouds around a mountain, they left him breathless with stone-hurling slings and spears.

sanskrit: vimuktakavacaḥ kruddho siktaḥ śoṇitavisravaiḥ sa puṣpakaṃ parityajya pṛthivyām avatiṣṭhata
english: His armor stripped away, enraged, drenched with streams of blood, he abandoned the Puṣpaka and stood upon the earth.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa kārmukī bāṇī pṛthivyāṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ labdhasaṃjño muhūrtena kruddhas tasthau yathāntakaḥ
english: Then the lord of rākṣasas, bow in hand, his arrows readied, having regained his senses after a moment, stood on the earth in fury like Death himself.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāśupataṃ divyam astraṃ saṃdhāya kārmuke tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti tān uktvā tac cāpaṃ vyapakarṣata
english: Then he fitted the divine Pāśupata weapon to his bow and, calling out to them "Stand! Stand!" drew that bow to its full extent.

sanskrit: jvālāmālī sa tu śaraḥ kravyādānugato raṇe mukto gulmān drumāṃś caiva bhasmakṛtvā pradhāvati
english: That arrow, wreathed in flames and followed by flesh-eating beings in battle, once released, reduced thickets and trees to ash as it blazed forth.

sanskrit: te tasya tejasā dagdhāḥ sainyā vaivasvatasya tu raṇe tasmin nipatitā dāvadagdhā nagā iva
english: The soldiers of Vaivasvata, scorched by its blazing power, fell upon that battlefield like trees burned down by a forest fire.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ rākṣaso bhīmavikramaḥ nanāda sumahānādaṃ kampayann iva medinīm
english: Then the rākṣasa of terrible valor, together with his ministers, let out a tremendous roar, shaking the earth as it were.
